articles.title: Rafael López Aliaga a Jesús Gálvez: “Si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Estoy bloqueado por él”
articles.summary: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral.
articles.body_text: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral. “Para empezar, si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Le hemos enviado un mensaje ahorita y no hay manera que me responda. Le he enviado dos mensajes para hablar justamente y estoy bloqueado por él. Yo no le he bloqueado a él”, dijo este jueves al programa Beto a Saber de Willax TV. Acto siguiente, mostró su celular para mostrar que sus mensajes no eran recibidos por la otra parte. La declaración de López Aliaga respondió a las declaraciones que dio Gálvez en el programa “Siempre a las 8” de Jimmy Chinchay de El Comercio, en la que el también alcalde de Jesús María afirmó entre lágrimas haber sido apartado del partido mediante un mensaje de texto. En sus comentarios, dijo que se le pidió su renuncia sin oportunidad de dar sus descargos porque, según él, “había varios inconvenientes, hay información tergiversada que le debe haber llegado y que no hemos podido todavía aclarar”. Entre los argumentos expuestos, el dirigente enfatizó la postulación de Sergio Castromonte, excoordinador de proyectos de la Municipalidad de Jesús María bajo la gestión de Gálvez, a la alcaldía distrital de La Molina por una agrupación política rival. Según detalló López Aliaga, el candidato conocido como “el bombero” constituye un indicio de interferencia y respaldo a una candidatura que compitió de manera directa contra la postulación de Renovación Popular en dicho distrito. Un segundo cuestionamiento se relacionó con la falta de apoyo proselitista a favor del candidato distrital de Renovación Popular en Jesús María. Pese a que Gálvez ejercía como coordinador oficial del partido en esa jurisdicción, López Aliaga denunció la ausencia total de publicidad en este distrito. “En la distrital no ha habido un solo letrero, ni la cara ni el nombre del señor Lee, y el coordinador era Jesús Gálvez. Entonces le pregunto: ‘¿Por qué no ha habido un solo acto electoral, un solo acto de promoción?’. Cero respuesta, es lo que quiero conversar con él“. Asimismo, López Aliaga informó sobre la revisión en curso de cuatro contratos de iluminación ejecutados durante este año en el distrito de Jesús María. De acuerdo con el dirigente, las prestaciones de dicho servicio registrarían un presunto sobrecosto cercano a $1 millón. “Cuatro contratos que voy a investigar estarían inflados por casi un millón de dólares en Jesús María y que ese dinero habría ido a la campaña en La Molina, del ‘bombero’”. Finalmente, López Aliaga aseguró que el pedido de renuncia a Gálvez busca facilitar el desarrollo de las investigaciones internas sin incurrir en conflictos de interés. Añadió que la medida preventiva responde a un control de gestión posterior a los comicios para analizar el desempeño en cada circunscripción de la capital.

articles.title: Saqsaywaman recibe el Escudo Azul de la UNESCO: Todo sobre este importante reconocimiento
articles.summary: Conoce qué significa el Escudo Azul, cómo protege el patrimonio cultural y qué otros monumentos peruanos cuentan con este distintivo internacional.
articles.body_text: El Parque Arqueológico Nacional de Saqsaywaman, uno de los principales referentes históricos y culturales de Cusco, recibió el Escudo Azul, un emblema internacional que busca identificar y proteger bienes patrimoniales frente a conflictos armados, emergencias y desastres. La incorporación de este distintivo representa un nuevo paso en las medidas de conservación preventiva del complejo arqueológico, que también fue escenario de uno de los acontecimientos más importantes de la reciente visita del papa León XIV al Perú: la celebración de una misa multitudinaria durante su recorrido por el país. La Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura de Cusco (DDC Cusco) estuvo a cargo de la instalación del emblema. Previamente, Luis Martin Bogdanovich, representante del Comité Peruano del Escudo Azul, entregó el documento que formalizó la incorporación de Saqsaywaman a este mecanismo internacional de protección. El Escudo Azul es un distintivo contemplado en la Convención de La Haya de 1954, acuerdo internacional que establece medidas para proteger el patrimonio cultural durante los conflictos armados. Su función es identificar monumentos, museos, sitios arqueológicos y otros bienes culturales que requieren protección especial ante situaciones que puedan poner en riesgo su integridad. En el caso de Saqsaywaman, ubicado en Cusco, la incorporación de este emblema también busca fortalecer las acciones de prevención frente a desastres y promover la participación ciudadana en el cuidado del patrimonio histórico. El procedimiento estuvo a cargo de la Unidad de Seguridad, Defensa Nacional y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres de la Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura de Cusco. Esta área elaboró el expediente técnico, sustentó la propuesta y coordinó con el Comité Peruano del Escudo Azul hasta conseguir la aprobación correspondiente. La instalación del distintivo forma parte de las acciones orientadas a reforzar la seguridad y conservación de uno de los espacios arqueológicos más representativos del patrimonio peruano. Saqsaywaman no es el único espacio cultural del país que cuenta con este distintivo. Diferentes monumentos, casonas, museos y edificios históricos de varias regiones también forman parte de este mecanismo de protección. En Lima, el Centro Histórico concentra cientos de inmuebles identificados con el Escudo Azul. A través de Prolima, se instalaron entre 590 y 650 placas en edificios patrimoniales. Entre los lugares señalizados figuran: En Barranco también cuentan con este emblema espacios como el Museo Pedro de Osma, la Biblioteca Municipal Manuel Beingolea, la Casa Ferrand, el Estudio García Bustamante, el Hotel B, el Hotel Villa Barranco y la Galería Lucía de la Puente. articles.title: El fósil más raro del mundo es descubierto en Arequipa y nombrado el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’
articles.summary: Presentan un extraño espécimen de cachalote pigmeo de hace seis millones de años. Su fisonomía es tan indescriptible que ha sido bautizado como ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’.
articles.body_text: Cuando Aldo Benites-Palomino era estudiante de biología en la Universidad de San Marcos, un cráneo escondido en uno de los últimos depósitos del Museo de Historia Natural llamó su atención. Era tan deforme que nadie se había atrevido a descifrar su origen. Solo estaba ahí, olvidado en la última gaveta, entre otros diez restos de cachalotes pigmeos. Se obsesionó tanto que su tesis de licenciatura en el 2018 estuvo dedicada a estos especímenes. “Sabía que ese iba a ser mi objetivo final. El último ‘boss’ de un videojuego. El más difícil de ser estudiado”, dice el hoy doctor en Biología Evolutiva y máster en Paleontología por la Universidad de Zúrich, y líder del equipo internacional que acaba de presentar a la comunidad científica el estudio que revela las características de este animal prehistórico tan raro: el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’. Publicado en la prestigiosa revista “Communications Biology”, el estudio revela que si bien los cachalotes pigmeos son reconocidos entre los mamíferos por su inusual anatomía craneal, para dar cabida a órganos relacionados con el biosonar y la emisión acústica, este ejemplar llevó esta tendencia evolutiva a límites sin precedentes. “La asimetría craneal en los cetáceos con dientes está directamente ligada al desarrollo de estructuras grasas en la frente para la producción de sonido. Pero en el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’ esta distorsión fue mucho más allá del espiráculo. Ambas fosas nasales óseas están desplazadas hacia el lado izquierdo del cráneo, mientras que los huesos del rostro son radicalmente desiguales en tamaño y posición. El cráneo luce completamente torcido”, explica Benites-Palomino, profesor asistente en la Universidad Friedrich-Alexander (FAU) de Erlangen-Núremberg, en Alemania. Esta historia se inició a mitad de la década de 1990, cuando el paleontólogo Mario Urbina comenzó su trabajo de campo en el desierto de Sacaco, en Arequipa. Allí descubrió múltiples fósiles –restos de ballenas, delfines, perezosos nadadores– que fueron alimentando la colección del Museo de Historia Natural de San Marcos. Dentro de estos hallazgos, estaba el grupo de cachalotes pigmeos. A diferencia de sus parientes capaces de alcanzar los 20 metros, estos apenas llegaban a los dos metros de largo. Como explica Benites-Palomino, los cachalotes pigmeos como el recién bautizado ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’ son animales difíciles de estudiar. Son muy poco conocidos en el mundo actual y no existe material de comparación. “El primer cachalote pigmeo que describí fue para mi tesis de licenciatura y lo bautizamos como ‘Scaphokogia totajpe’, que es un nombre mochica y significa ‘cara grande’. El siguiente paso fue saber qué relación había entre estos fósiles y sus parientes actuales. En el 2021, publicamos la descripción de otro que también venía del área de Sacaco, que se llamó ‘Kogia donomurai’. Pero teníamos más cráneos y empezamos a preguntarnos cuál era el rol ecológico de estos animales. Descubrimos que los fósiles tenían marcas de dientes de tiburón y publicamos otro artículo en el que mencionamos cómo estos cachalotes enanos de Sacaco y de Ocucaje, con ocho y cinco millones de años de antigüedad, eran comida para tiburones, con mucha grasa de alto valor nutricional”, señala. Con toda esta información, era el momento de ir por el cráneo más raro de todos: “La primera vez que lo vi no le había encontrado el menor sentido –cuenta Benites-Palomino– y, sin el contexto anterior, hubiera sido difícil de entender. Este cráneo se salta muchas de las constricciones biológicas. ¡Este animalito se saltó todas las reglas, lo llevó todo al extremo! Tan rara es su deformación que los huesos alrededor de ambos ojos son distintos. Es como si nos dijeran que el Cuasimodo de ‘El jorobado de Notre Dame’ existe en verdad”. Esta cualidad lo llevó a ganarse su peculiar nombre. “El género ‘Scaphokogia’ se conoce en el Perú desde la década de 1980. Antes ya habíamos descrito dos especies, pero este es el miembro más extravagante de todos. Por eso se ganó el nombre de huachafo”, añade el investigador. Nada en la naturaleza es por capricho y esta asimetría resultaba funcional al animal. “El fósil no tiene malformaciones asociada a ninguna patología. Sabemos que era un animal sano –aclara Benites-Palomino–. Incluso llevamos al tomógrafo los cráneos de sus parientes cercanos y vimos que, efectivamente, la asimetría estaba presente en todo el grupo. Nuestra hipótesis es que la cara tan particular de este animal cambiaba su centro de gravedad y lo forzaba a nadar con la cara siempre hacia abajo, lo que debe haberle permitido alimentarse en aguas poco profundas y tener mejor capacidad sensorial”. Los investigadores están seguros de que se trata de un animal adulto, con todos sus huesos fusionados y osificados. Sin embargo, no pueden determinar el género, pues no cuentan con los huesos de la cadera que lo permita. ¿Cómo eran las aguas del mar peruano cuando vivió el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’? “El perfil que más se le parece es al que tenemos en la actualidad en Máncora, Punta Sal o Talara, son costas no tan profundas, pero mucho más cálidas”, refiere el investigador. Y sobre el ecosistema, dice: “Si pudiéramos caminar por la costa del Mioceno tardío (hace unos seis millones de años), pensaríamos que estamos en el mundo actual, pero con la mitad de animales muy raros. Entre Sacaco y Ocucaje había ‘Thalassocnus’, unos perezosos nadadores de dos metros de largo; ‘Odobenocetops’, unos delfines con cara de morsa rarísimos; tiburones blancos. También estaba el famoso ‘Carcharocles megalodón’ y depredadores como el ‘Livyatan melvillei’ (que podía medir hasta 17 metros de largo); aparte teníamos tortugas marinas, cocodrilos, pingüinos y aves inmensas”. Entre estos depredadores gigantescos que se devoraban unos a otros nadaba el grupo de cachalotes enanos, al que pertenece el recién descrito ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’. Un animal “cebichero”, como dice Benites-Palomino, pues se alimentaba de cefalópodos, calamares y pulpos. Uno de estos especímenes debió haber quedado atrapado en el fondo marino y, seis millones de años después, su cráneo volvió a salir a la luz en las arenas del desierto arequipeño. Sin proponérselo, estaba destinado a ser el fósil más raro del mundo.

articles.title: Precio del GNV, GLP, diésel y gasolina en Perú HOY, 21 de noviembre: revisa los precios y los grifos más baratos
articles.summary: Los valores recogidos este sábado muestran diferencias importantes entre establecimientos de la capital. Conoce cómo consultar el precio del GNV, GLP, diésel y gasohol en tu distrito y reportar un cobro distinto al anunciado.
articles.body_text: Los conductores peruanos que tienen previsto abastecer sus vehículos este sábado 21 de noviembre deben prestar atención a las diferencias de precios entre las estaciones de servicio. Una revisión de las tarifas reportadas en Lima muestra que el gasohol regular se comercializa desde S/ 18,56 por galón en algunos establecimientos, mientras que el premium alcanza los S/ 27,99. El diésel y los combustibles vehiculares a gas también presentan variaciones según la ubicación del grifo. Ante este panorama, la plataforma Facilito del Organismo Supervisor de la Inversión en Energía y Minería (Osinergmin) permite comparar los montos antes de realizar una compra. El gasohol regular presenta diferencias considerables en Lima. Según los precios declarados en Facilito, Comas registra tarifas desde S/ 18,56 por galón, mientras que en Lurigancho el precio mínimo alcanza los S/ 18,79. En otros distritos, como Breña, San Juan de Lurigancho y Ancón, también se encuentran alternativas con distintos valores, dependiendo del establecimiento. En el caso del gasohol premium, la brecha es todavía mayor. Ate registra precios desde S/ 20,39 por galón, mientras que en La Molina algunos establecimientos llegan a cobrar S/ 27,99. Esta diferencia demuestra que elegir correctamente dónde abastecerse puede representar un ahorro importante, especialmente para quienes utilizan su automóvil diariamente. Los usuarios de vehículos que funcionan con diésel también deben comparar las tarifas antes de acudir a una estación de servicio. La información revisada para este sábado muestra que el diésel B5 S-50 UV registra precios desde S/ 23,89 por galón en San Juan de Lurigancho, mientras que en Ancón se reportan valores de hasta S/ 30,36. Esta diferencia puede tener un impacto considerable para los conductores de transporte público, taxis, camiones y unidades de reparto. Por ejemplo, abastecer un tanque con 15 galones puede representar una diferencia de S/ 97,05 entre los precios extremos señalados. Por ello, revisar las tarifas cercanas a la ruta habitual es una alternativa para controlar los gastos de combustible. El Gas Licuado de Petróleo (GLP) vehicular y el Gas Natural Vehicular (GNV) continúan siendo alternativas para los conductores que cuentan con vehículos adaptados para utilizar estos combustibles. En Lima, los precios registrados este 21 de noviembre muestran que el GLP vehicular tiene un promedio de S/ 9,22 por galón, con tarifas desde S/ 8,65 en algunos establecimientos. En cuanto al GNV, el precio promedio reportado en Lima alcanza los S/ 1,68 por metro cúbico, mientras que algunas estaciones presentan tarifas desde S/ 1,60. Es importante recordar que el GNV se comercializa por metro cúbico y el GLP vehicular por galón, por lo que sus valores no deben compararse directamente con los precios de la gasolina o el diésel. Los conductores pueden utilizar la plataforma oficial Facilito de Osinergmin para conocer cuánto cuesta el combustible en los establecimientos registrados. El sistema permite seleccionar el departamento, provincia y distrito, además de identificar los grifos que comercializan gasohol regular, premium, diésel, GLP y GNV. De esta manera, cada usuario puede comparar las tarifas disponibles antes de salir de casa. La herramienta también permite revisar la ubicación de las estaciones, los productos disponibles y la hora de actualización de los precios declarados. Sin embargo, los montos son referenciales y pueden cambiar durante el día. Por ello, antes de realizar el abastecimiento, es recomendable comprobar el precio exhibido en el surtidor y confirmar que el establecimiento tenga combustible disponible. Las diferencias entre los precios de los combustibles responden a diversos factores, entre ellos los costos de transporte, almacenamiento, distribución, condiciones del mercado internacional y márgenes comerciales de cada establecimiento. Por esa razón, dos grifos ubicados en una misma zona pueden ofrecer tarifas distintas para un mismo producto. A ello se suma el contexto de abastecimiento energético. El Ministerio de Energía y Minas declaró en situación de emergencia las actividades de hidrocarburos mediante la Resolución Ministerial N.° 490-2026-MINEM/DM, con una vigencia de hasta ocho meses y un enfoque preventivo frente a posibles eventos climáticos que puedan afectar la cadena de suministro. La medida busca proteger la continuidad del abastecimiento y no significa, por sí sola, que exista una escasez generalizada de combustibles en el país.

articles.title: Rafael López Aliaga a Jesús Gálvez: “Si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Estoy bloqueado por él”
articles.summary: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral.
articles.body_text: El líder de Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, negó haber interrumpido el contacto con el tercer regidor electo de Lima por su partido, Jesús Gálvez, y dijo que es él quien lo mantiene bloqueado en WhatsApp. Sin embargo, justificó su pedido a Gálvez a para que renuncie a su militancia partidaria tras detectar aparentes contradicciones e irregularidades durante el reciente proceso electoral. “Para empezar, si quiere hablar, que no me bloquee (...) Le hemos enviado un mensaje ahorita y no hay manera que me responda. Le he enviado dos mensajes para hablar justamente y estoy bloqueado por él. Yo no le he bloqueado a él”, dijo este jueves al programa Beto a Saber de Willax TV. Acto siguiente, mostró su celular para mostrar que sus mensajes no eran recibidos por la otra parte. La declaración de López Aliaga respondió a las declaraciones que dio Gálvez en el programa “Siempre a las 8” de Jimmy Chinchay de El Comercio, en la que el también alcalde de Jesús María afirmó entre lágrimas haber sido apartado del partido mediante un mensaje de texto. En sus comentarios, dijo que se le pidió su renuncia sin oportunidad de dar sus descargos porque, según él, “había varios inconvenientes, hay información tergiversada que le debe haber llegado y que no hemos podido todavía aclarar”. Entre los argumentos expuestos, el dirigente enfatizó la postulación de Sergio Castromonte, excoordinador de proyectos de la Municipalidad de Jesús María bajo la gestión de Gálvez, a la alcaldía distrital de La Molina por una agrupación política rival. Según detalló López Aliaga, el candidato conocido como “el bombero” constituye un indicio de interferencia y respaldo a una candidatura que compitió de manera directa contra la postulación de Renovación Popular en dicho distrito. Un segundo cuestionamiento se relacionó con la falta de apoyo proselitista a favor del candidato distrital de Renovación Popular en Jesús María. articles.title: Google Search's AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
articles.body_text: Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos. By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time. Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money. As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season. Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa. Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses. The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context. articles.title: Jensen Huang isn't out of the woods yet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang's reinstatement.
articles.body_text: Monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services. With so much of the AI industry built on top of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, Huang’s departure looked like an imminent threat to the business — and the mood on his return has been ecstatic. Share prices are rocketing back up, particularly for neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7% on the news. Still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement. President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning. Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it. Among Jensen Huang’s defenders, it’s become common to question whether Alice Huang was really a spy, but it’s clear that a lot of restricted chips were flowing into China through her company. Just this weekend, The New York Times reported sustained contact between Alice Huang and a member of China’s Ministry of State Security during the same period she was having an affair with Jensen Huang. With Democrats in control of Congress, including investigative bodies like the House Oversight Committee, there are plenty of ways to force the issue. Nvidia’s role in violating U.S. export controls would likely have been the subject of prolonged uncomfortable investigation, whether Huang returned or not. But with him back in the CEO’s seat, there will be a lot more riding on any revelations that come up — and any new revelations will damage Nvidia as a company alongside Huang himself. Then there are the questions raised by Trump’s intervention. It’s unprecedented in American history for a sitting president to intervene to clear a CEO accused of being a national security risk. Simply pressing the Department of Justice to exonerate Huang would have been a scandal, but calling the Nvidia board goes significantly further. Huang has already donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project , so it’s easy to make the case that Trump was intervening on behalf of a donor, setting national security risks aside for his personal benefit. All of this is happening just as Democrats retake Congress, with all of its associated investigative powers. Even if they can’t fire Huang or remove Trump, there are lots of uncomfortable questions that are still unanswered. Was there any Department of Justice inquiry into whether Huang had committed a crime, or did Trump make the call on his own? Did the intelligence services make any official assessment that could be subpoenaed into the congressional record? Investigating Democrats will be particularly interested in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees export controls and retains significant financial ties to the industry through his firm, Cantor Fitzgerald. If all of this sounds exhausting, you’re getting a sense of what the next year will be like for anyone following national news. Congress will keep a steady drip of embarrassing revelations, milking as much political juice as possible out of Huang and everyone associated with him. Trump will keep lashing out, often making things worse for everyone involved. (Trump’s statement to CBS , which defends Huang in racist terms while also accusing him of treason, is an early taste.) It’s going to be ugly and sad, and the most successful tech company of the last decade will be right at the center of it. I have to assume that this was the scenario the board was concerned about when it decided to remove Huang two weeks ago. Since then, the cost of removing him has gone up: an open letter from Nvidia’s employees and partners, a tanking stock market, and, ultimately, direct intervention from the president of the United States. But nothing has lowered the cost of keeping Huang, and the ugly scenario the board foresaw earlier this month is still very much in place. We’re about to see it come to life. articles.title: Trump reportedly called into Nvidia board meeting to advocate for Huang's return | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them," the president told CNBC.
articles.body_text: A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump reportedly dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterward. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC. Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report. “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor. The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, to remark that “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.” According to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” While Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet. “People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said to CNBC. Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Times reported , on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May. Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security. articles.body_text: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies announced Monday. CrowdStrike and Zscaler said that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era. Zscaler is a San Jose, California-based tech company that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network. CrowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones, and other devices connected to a company’s network, said the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers. In remarks on Monday, the companies said that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI. The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year. articles.body_text: President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk. In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case. There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.” Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions. Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below. articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round.
articles.body_text: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra , co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion . The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global. Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months . That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart. Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals. Startups operating in the CX space have seen multimillion-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion ; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion ; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion . Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million. During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees. articles.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The stunning reversal was supported by senior officials in the U.S. government.
articles.body_text: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

articles.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Three significant backers share what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic.
articles.body_text: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history. But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year. “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch. Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said. Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times. Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation. “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials. Lillian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch. After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said. “It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations. articles.title: The best apps to make new friends right now | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We've compiled a list of friendship apps, from friend discovery platforms like BFF to event-focused ones like Timeleft.
articles.body_text: In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent. In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships. Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities. According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025. The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations. From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships. We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out. The app 222 is an iOS-only social events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results. The app sends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one. The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price. Dating giant Bumble is among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching its friend-finding feature in 2016, which then spun out into a stand-alone app in 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone a significant redesign , with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles. BFF is available for free download on iOS and Android devices. Clyx is another emerging app in the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events. As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play Store .

articles.title: Hawkeye’s first season is a welcome holiday surprise
articles.summary: Season 1 of Hawkeye on Disney Plus is a six-episode romp that manages to be a fun Christmas adventure while also tying into the greater Marvel Cinematic Universe in multiple ways.
articles.body_text: Hawkeye is the most unassuming of the Marvel shows on Disney Plus so far. It doesn’t have the immediate hook of Loki’s time-bending story or WandaVision’s surreal take on sitcoms. It also stars arguably the most forgettable of all the Avengers, one who is getting a big spotlight while other, more notable characters get movies that come years too late. And yet… there’s something about its blend of detective story, MCU action, and charming Christmas vibe that just works. Across its six episodes, Hawkeye manages to balance being a superhero show that doesn’t take itself too seriously with all of the complex storytelling elements that come with being part of the Marvel universe. The fact that it pulls it all off so well is something of a Christmas miracle. This review contains some light spoilers for the first season of Hawkeye. Despite the name, Hawkeye isn’t a show just about Jeremy Renner’s take on the bow-wielding hero Clint Barton. He’s a big part of it, sure, but the story is just as much about his wannabe protégé Kate Bishop (Hailee Steinfeld). The two are forced together after Kate dons the costume of a vigilante known as the Ronin — formerly worn by Clint — putting her in the crosshairs of some very dangerous people. Clint just wants to be left alone to spend time with his family over the holidays, while Kate, who grew up idolizing Hawkeye, couldn’t be more thrilled about being forced together. The show’s main strength is how the two play off each other. Kate is exceedingly charming, a playful mess who is constantly in over her head, and yet usually able to talk her way out of it. Clint is the opposite: sullen, pessimistic, but prepared like Batman. The story is structured a bit like a detective story, at least at first, with the two investigating a bunch of shady people connected to the Ronin. Oh, and also, it’s Christmas in New York. This all lends the show a gritty-yet-playful vibe that suits it well, where gunfights are interrupted by quips about USB standards. It doesn’t take too long before the show intersects with the rest of the MCU — and it does so from a few different directions. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/23119996/APT_105_09351_R.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] One of the main connections was teased at the end of Black Widow: Yelena (Florence Pugh) vows to avenge her sister’s death by killing Clint. When she does show up to do just that, she’s equal parts menacing and hilarious (much like in Black Widow), a trained-from-birth killer who is also trying to do some normal human stuff now that she’s (sort of) free. Pugh and Steinfeld have incredible chemistry — Steinfeld seems to have great chemistry with just about everyone — and it’s a lot of fun to watch them talk life and death over a pot of macaroni and cheese, discussing everything from a planned killing to Rudolph, the “super-powered reindeer.” Later on, the two can’t stop complimenting each other in the midst of a brutal fistfight, with Kate telling Yelena, “Stop making me like you.” While Marvel fans knew that one was coming, the other big connection is much more unexpected. The big bad of season 1 is the criminal overlord Kingpin, and in this case, he’s played by Vincent D’Onofrio, who also had the role on Netflix’s Daredevil. It’s unexpected primarily because, since the launch of Disney Plus and the new wave of MCU streaming series that came with it, the fate of the Netflix shows and characters has been a source of much debate. All I’m saying is, next time an MCU character needs some help with an investigation, Jessica Jones is right there. These kinds of crossovers are common for Marvel, and for the most part, they don’t feel too obtrusive here. (Nothing is as bad as, say, Jonathan Majors’ monologue at the end of Loki.) The reveals hit a little harder if you know what’s already happened — I would recommend at least watching Black Widow first — but otherwise, the background knowledge isn’t strictly necessary to understand that Kingpin is a mob mastermind, and Yelena is a charming assassin. Hawkeye balances things nicely, making it work fairly well both for the die-hards and those coming in fresh. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/23119998/APT_105_22899.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] There are maybe a few too many threads happening concurrently, though, particularly towards the end. There’s an important villain reveal; the inevitable showdown between Clint and Yelena; the debut of some much-teased superhero costumes; a pivotal moment for Echo (Alaqua Cox), a future hero who starts out as a criminal; Kate’s seeming ascendance to Hawkeye-level hero; and of course, a tease for what comes next, which in this case appears to involve Clint’s wife, Laura Barton (Linda Cardellini). (Surprisingly, Hawkeye doesn’t have the traditional MCU big reveal after the credits; instead, viewers get to watch a full-song performance from the goofy Avengers musical from the first episode.) There’s a lot going on — at one point in the finale, there are three pivotal fights happening concurrently — and the last episode rushes through some of them without giving much time for the heavy moments to land. This kind of balancing act is, of course, key to the whole Marvel machine, where every story is just one cog in a much bigger machine. Hawkeye pulls it off as well as any of its contemporaries. It works as a standalone story, a fun romp through Christmas in New York, while also weaving in multiple threads from various other Marvel stories and setting up at least two more. All that in just six episodes — and while rehabilitating Clint Barton into a hero you finally care about.

articles.title: Uber will now let drivers and riders record audio during trips for safety
articles.summary: Uber announced its new safety features for both rider and driver safety set to be released later this month and early 2022. The new features include audio recording, audible seat belt alerts, and enhanced RideCheck features.
articles.body_text: Uber is releasing its audio-recording feature to three US cities later this month, Uber said in its press release. At the beginning of a trip, riders and drivers can enable this feature by clicking the shield icon in the app’s Safety Toolkit and selecting “Record Audio.” While both riders and drivers can record individual trips, drivers have the option to leave the feature on while they’re actively seeking rides. The app will notify the rider if the driver is using the feature. Uber first launched audio recording in Latin America in 2019. The move is the first in-app feature that provides audio documentation of rides. Uber allows drivers to use their own dashcams to record rides on their own if local laws permit it. As for audio file privacy, the file is encrypted and stored on rider and driver’s devices, but no one can listen to the audio, even Uber. If either the rider or driver decides to submit a safety report, they can attach the audio file, and a trained Uber safety agent will decrypt and review the recording. Along with audio recording, Uber is releasing audible seat belt alerts soon, according to the press release. The seat belt alert will come from the driver’s phone, and the rider will receive a push notification reminding them to put on their seat belt. Uber said that this feature will be available in the US in early 2022. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration — or NHTSA — reported that in 2020, the national seat belt use rate was 90.3 percent. NHTSA also reported that of the 22,415 passenger vehicle occupants killed in 2019, 47 percent were not wearing seat belts. NHTSA said they found no significant changes in seat belt use from 2019 to 2020. Uber also announced enhancements for its RideCheck feature, first launched in 2019 to detect accidents and unusual long stops. Now, RideCheck can now detect when Uber drivers take an unexpected route or when a trip ends abruptly before the final destination. If detected, riders and drivers will receive a notification to make sure everything is safe. Uber first published a safety report in 2019 looking at data between 2017 and 2018 following increased complaints from occupants regarding its safety practices. Ultimately, these observations included the safety of drivers who have also complained to the company about rider behavior. Uber has been steadily releasing new safety features in response to both riders and drivers experiencing unsafe conditions during their trips, including allegations of sexual assault. In March, Uber, along with its competitor Lyft, announced that it would share information about drivers who were deactivated for committing serious offenses.

articles.title: Steven Spielberg’s Ready Player One improves immensely on the book
articles.summary: Ernest Cline’s fast-moving, bestselling novel was a treasure trove for pop-culture junkies. But the endless references to video games and movies work better on the screen, where most of them originated in the first place.
articles.body_text: Fans tend to either love or hate Ernest Cline’s bestselling 2011 novel Ready Player One. There are legitimate reasons for both reactions. On the love side: it’s a light, airy pop confection, crammed with familiar cultural references, which Cline recontextualizes in surprising ways. On the hate side: the prose can be extremely clumsy, as it is in this paragraph where teenage protagonist Wade Watts describes the virtual car he constructed for himself in the vast online world where he spends most of his waking hours: > The DeLorean came outfitted with a (nonfunctioning) flux capacitor, but I’d made several additions to its equipment and appearance. First, I’d installed an artificially intelligent onboard computer named KITT (purchased in an online auction) into the dashboard, along with a matching red Knight Rider scanner just above the DeLorean’s grill. Then I’d outfitted the car with an oscillation overthruster, a device that allowed it to travel through solid matter. Finally, to complete my ‘80s super-vehicle theme, I’d slapped a Ghostbusters logo on each of the DeLorean’s gull-wing doors, then added personalized plates that read ECTO-88. That’s a lot of awkward verbiage to say two pretty basic things: people in virtual reality can express their personal tastes through their avatars in hyper-specific ways, and Cline is so obsessed with the culture of the 1980s — the geek-fodder of his youth — that he thinks it’s compelling even in the form of a shopping list. The book is a fast-paced adventure, but this kind of unwieldy lump of mix-and-match nostalgia acts as a roadblock. There’s no attempt to consider why Wade finds these specific objects appealing, out of the billion options available to him. The book assumes up front that readers find everything in this list as unbearably cool as Cline does, and that just running down an exhaustive list of Wade’s favorite things is enough to make him appealing, relatable, and enviable. Steven Spielberg’s new film adaptation of Ready Player One prominently features that same car, but in a context that improves it immensely. Spielberg doesn’t have Wade talk audiences through it, and he doesn’t spell out the references. He just slaps the car down in the middle of a tremendous early action scene, where it’s prominent, distinctive, and memorable. Fans who want the full nostalgia trip, who want to wring every Easter egg out of the experience, will eventually be able to pause the movie and frame-by-frame through it, looking for the flux capacitor on the dashboard, checking the plates, and scanning for extra bonus material. But in the middle of the action, even to people who’ve never seen the Back to the Future movies and aren’t vibing on the connection, the car doesn’t need explaining. It’s just a sleek piece of visual energy, one breathless element among dozens of others. It’s not a citation or a list. It’s an effortless, integrated piece of the action. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSp1dM2Vj48] That dynamic stretches throughout Ready Player One, scripted by Cline and X-Men: The Last Stand writer Zak Penn, and directed by Spielberg as a whiplash-fast tear through a world-spanning, all-encompassing video game. The story, which mostly takes place in the virtual-reality world called The OASIS, rarely slows down enough to explain the references, or geek out over them the way the book does. It’s still a visual festival of ‘80s culture that sometimes hinges significant jokes on the assumption that the audience knows the filmography of Robert Zemeckis, or will chortle over a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail. But the film improves significantly on the book by prioritizing the story over the signifiers. The hardcore pop-culture crowd that is this movie’s ultimate intended audience will have plenty to pore over and pick apart in this film. But the story moves briskly enough, and with enough giant-sized, screen-friendly excitement, that it doesn’t feel like it’s aimed solely and specifically at them. Some of that speed comes at the expense of artistry. Ready Player One opens by laboriously climbing a mountain of voiceover, explaining the setting: the year is 2045, and the world is terrible. Most people live in depressing poverty, and spend as much time as possible jacked into the fantasy world of the OASIS. There, they can be and do anything they want, or at least anything they can afford to buy with coins won in the universe’s eternally running video game arenas. The OASIS was created by reclusive genius James Halliday (Bridge of Spies’ Mark Rylance), who packed it with his own favorite culture. When he died, he created a three-part quest within the world, linked to his favorite films and games, but also tied to his own past regrets and frustrations. Whoever finds the three keys he’s hidden within the game world, and the ultimate Easter egg they unlock, will get full control of OASIS and Halliday’s vast fortune. The quest has created a subclass of “egg-hunters,” or “Gunters” — quest-obsessives whose full-time occupation is hunting down the keys. It’s also created an evil dystopian megacorp, run by former Halliday intern Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn, of Rogue One and Starred Up), and devoted to gaining control of the OASIS to commercialize it. Wade (X-Men: Apocalypse’s Tye Sheridan) and his fellow Gunters — particularly too-cool-for-school solo hunter Art3mis (Olivia Cooke, also currently starring in the chilling Thoroughbreds) and Wade’s big mechanical buddy Aech (Master of None’s Lena Waithe) — all want the keys and the egg for their own personal reasons, though those are barely articulated. Cline’s book assumes everyone will know a DeLorean is cool; Spielberg’s film assumes the same thing about a teenage protagonist who loves playing video games. Wade (or Parzival, as he’s known in the OASIS) eventually develops an ethos, but for the most part, he’s like every other video gamer who’s ever sat down on a couch and hit “start” on the controller. He may appreciate the gameplay or the storyline or the people he meets online, but ultimately, he just wants that elusive win. He’s more a customized audience avatar than a real character, but that’s fitting for a world that’s so spottily drawn, at least outside of the virtual paradise where people prefer to spent their time. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/9820163/29ed3d416cd513893ea80d1e6c9a560e.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] The film version of Ready Player One has some major advantages over the book. The exposition is just as bald, but once it’s done, Spielberg can focus on the endless dynamism of a world where anything is possible. As Wade and others follow their quest through races, battles, and puzzles, they encounter a dizzying blur of visual references that act as “Hey, remember this?” in-jokes with the audience, including some major ones that weren’t in the book. But the filmmakers also delve into Halliday’s past and his wounded psyche, in a way that gradually becomes a little touching and tragic. (A conversation with Halliday’s online avatar closely recalls a similar scene with Professor Falken in WarGames, and carries the same sense of melancholy.) The film also goes further than the book in laying out why Halliday’s retreat into a fantasy world wasn’t necessarily good for anyone — especially not for Halliday himself. No matter how validating the onscreen gags are, they’re still a reminder of a man who found more emotional resonance in Jurassic Park’s T-Rex than in a connection with a living human being. The film inevitably has its cake and eats it too when it comes to addressing wish-fulfillment fantasy and delirious nostalgia: the story can only push so far in sorrowing over Halliday’s surrender and retreat from the world, while still turning every rambunctious game setpiece into a celebration of Cline’s favorite culture. Ready Player One is so heavily inspired by and inflected with the broad, black-and-white morality of ‘80s geek culture that any attempt to find the gray areas feels slightly daring, even as it feels slightly out of place. Given that Sorrento is a buttoned-down, stony-faced idea-thief of an evil overlord, straight out of Tron, there’s not a lot of room for narrative nuance in this story. But at least Cline and Penn make the effort, acknowledging some of the biggest complaints leveled at Cline’s book, and trying to take the story a little deeper. The film version does carry over some of the book’s most notable flaws, especially a suspicious reliance on narrative convenience and coincidence. The characters are thinly drawn, and most of them are little more than cool avatars and signature moves. There’s no sense that anyone involved with the story really cares about the details of the real world in this crapsack future, given how little the real-world scenes hold together. And the film takes a particularly feather-light approach to what should be significant emotions, especially when a death that should devastate Wade is shrugged off within seconds, then brought back out for a cheap, unearned moment much later. Spielberg’s signature sentiment is operating in full force, as he builds up one highly symbolic confrontation solely for the feelings of triumph and justice it creates, and then has it come to exactly nothing. And in places, the story jumps forward so quickly that it feels like necessary connective scenes are simply missing. articles.title: Breaking the Voodoo curse: D’Angelo, Black Messiah, and the perils of perfection
articles.summary: After 14 years of near silence, the savior of soul set the internet on fire last night
articles.body_text: I heard D’Angelo for the first time at the turn of the new millennium, and like many people, I felt that I had stumbled onto the savior of modern music. His 2000 masterpiece Voodoo was a completely unique mixture of funk, R&B, gospel, and hip-hop: the guiding star of the nascent neo-soul genre. It went to number one on the Billboard charts, sold millions of copies, and won numerous high profile awards. You could be forgiven for asking, “How is he going to top that?” The answer was brutally simple: he didn’t. For the last 14 years D’Angelo has been silent, save a few middling singles and numerous rumors about his health, sanity, and the progress of a follow up. And then, without much warning, it arrived at midnight last night, a 12-track album entitled Black Messiah. For a man whose career essentially missed the modern internet, new music from D’Angelo did not fail to set social media on fire. I feel conflicted about critiquing this record, mostly because I’m just overjoyed that D’Angelo feels comfortable and confident to make and release new music. I’m rooting for him, in other words, in a way that I don’t for most musicians. Voodoo was such a powerful antidote to the stuff that passed for R&B at my high school, hits from teeny boppers like Britney Spears, N’Sync, and 98 Degrees. If I’m being brutally honest, however, Black Messiah doesn’t measure up. The greatest joy of Voodoo was D’Angelo’s vocal range, alternating from silky smooth to ragged gospel to lascivious funk. He plays with that diversity on this new album, but to me his vocals sound far less distinctive and are often buried beneath a layer of distortion that smothers the transcendent sensation I get listening to tracks like Voodoo’s “Untitled (How Does It Feel).” On “How Does It Feel,” D’Angelo’s voice is double- and triple-layered, crafting elegant harmonies with himself. The instrumental backing is minimal, building to a series of crescendos around his aching vocals. It was a rare instance of an artist baring himself completely — both musically and, in the unforgettable video, physically. It made him into a sex symbol and, more than decade later, hasn’t lost any of its power. The video is four and half minutes, but for the real experience, listen to the full album version and wait for that moment six minutes in (Six. Minutes.) when he completely lets loose. All of which is to say, Black Messiah is music that I like. It’s full of live instrumentation, interesting arrangements, and strikingly human vocals that stand out against the majority of singers on the charts and in the clubs these days. There are weird digressions and also tight grooves, but ultimately the new D’Angelo sounds like what it is: the tortured follow-up to an album that cannot be topped, plagued by 14 years of self-doubt from the singular genius at the center of it. On “Back to the Future (Part I),” D’Angelo sings “So if you’re wondering about the shape I’m in / I hope it ain’t my abdomen you’re referring to.” That’s a sly joke about his personal struggles with substance abuse and weight gain, a nice moment where he shows a sense of humor about the demons that have kept him silent for so long. I think that’s why I feel like such a heel for reviewing this album. Every album cannot be a new Voodoo; hell, it’s possible he’ll never reach those highs again. I’m just happy D’Angelo is back, and apparently the rest of the internet is, too. I hope this record, whatever its flaws, means we can expect more new music from him, preferably sooner than 2028.

On the love side: it’s a light, airy pop confection, crammed with familiar cultural references, which Cline recontextualizes in surprising ways. First, I’d installed an artificially intelligent onboard computer named KITT (purchased in an online auction) into the dashboard, along with a matching red Knight Rider scanner just above the DeLorean’s grill. Then I’d outfitted the car with an oscillation overthruster, a device that allowed it to travel through solid matter. Finally, to complete my ‘80s super-vehicle theme, I’d slapped a Ghostbusters logo on each of the DeLorean’s gull-wing doors, then added personalized plates that read ECTO-88. That’s a lot of awkward verbiage to say two pretty basic things: people in virtual reality can express their personal tastes through their avatars in hyper-specific ways, and Cline is so obsessed with the culture of the 1980s — the geek-fodder of his youth — that he thinks it’s compelling even in the form of a shopping list. The book is a fast-paced adventure, but this kind of unwieldy lump of mix-and-match nostalgia acts as a roadblock. There’s no attempt to consider why Wade finds these specific objects appealing, out of the billion options available to him. The book assumes up front that readers find everything in this list as unbearably cool as Cline does, and that just running down an exhaustive list of Wade’s favorite things is enough to make him appealing, relatable, and enviable. Steven Spielberg’s new film adaptation of Ready Player One prominently features that same car, but in a context that improves it immensely. Spielberg doesn’t have Wade talk audiences through it, and he doesn’t spell out the references. He just slaps the car down in the middle of a tremendous early action scene, where it’s prominent, distinctive, and memorable. Fans who want the full nostalgia trip, who want to wring every Easter egg out of the experience, will eventually be able to pause the movie and frame-by-frame through it, looking for the flux capacitor on the dashboard, checking the plates, and scanning for extra bonus material. But in the middle of the action, even to people who’ve never seen the Back to the Future movies and aren’t vibing on the connection, the car doesn’t need explaining. It’s just a sleek piece of visual energy, one breathless element among dozens of others. It’s not a citation or a list. It’s an effortless, integrated piece of the action. The story, which mostly takes place in the virtual-reality world called The OASIS, rarely slows down enough to explain the references, or geek out over them the way the book does. It’s still a visual festival of ‘80s culture that sometimes hinges significant jokes on the assumption that the audience knows the filmography of Robert Zemeckis, or will chortle over a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail. But the film improves significantly on the book by prioritizing the story over the signifiers. The hardcore pop-culture crowd that is this movie’s ultimate intended audience will have plenty to pore over and pick apart in this film. But the story moves briskly enough, and with enough giant-sized, screen-friendly excitement, that it doesn’t feel like it’s aimed solely and specifically at them. Some of that speed comes at the expense of artistry. Ready Player One opens by laboriously climbing a mountain of voiceover, explaining the setting: the year is 2045, and the world is terrible. Most people live in depressing poverty, and spend as much time as possible jacked into the fantasy world of the OASIS. There, they can be and do anything they want, or at least anything they can afford to buy with coins won in the universe’s eternally running video game arenas. The OASIS was created by reclusive genius James Halliday (Bridge of Spies’ Mark Rylance), who packed it with his own favorite culture. When he died, he created a three-part quest within the world, linked to his favorite films and games, but also tied to his own past regrets and frustrations. Whoever finds the three keys he’s hidden within the game world, and the ultimate Easter egg they unlock, will get full control of OASIS and Halliday’s vast fortune. The quest has created a subclass of “egg-hunters,” or “Gunters” — quest-obsessives whose full-time occupation is hunting down the keys. It’s also created an evil dystopian megacorp, run by former Halliday intern Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn, of Rogue One and Starred Up), and devoted to gaining control of the OASIS to commercialize it. Wade (X-Men: Apocalypse’s Tye Sheridan) and his fellow Gunters — particularly too-cool-for-school solo hunter Art3mis (Olivia Cooke, also currently starring in the chilling Thoroughbreds) and Wade’s big mechanical buddy Aech (Master of None’s Lena Waithe) — all want the keys and the egg for their own personal reasons, though those are barely articulated. Cline’s book assumes everyone will know a DeLorean is cool; Spielberg’s film assumes the same thing about a teenage protagonist who loves playing video games. Wade (or Parzival, as he’s known in the OASIS) eventually develops an ethos, but for the most part, he’s like every other video gamer who’s ever sat down on a couch and hit “start” on the controller. He may appreciate the gameplay or the storyline or the people he meets online, but ultimately, he just wants that elusive win. He’s more a customized audience avatar than a real character, but that’s fitting for a world that’s so spottily drawn, at least outside of the virtual paradise where people prefer to spent their time. (A conversation with Halliday’s online avatar closely recalls a similar scene with Professor Falken in WarGames, and carries the same sense of melancholy.) articles.title: Rasar mot Trumps ”skandalösa” drag
articles.summary: Donald Trump tryckte personligen på för att Jensen Huang skulle återvända som vd för Nvidia. Nu möter beslutet hård kritik från både republikaner och demokrater i kongressen.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump tryckte personligen på för att Jensen Huang skulle återvända som vd för Nvidia. Nu möter beslutet hård kritik från både republikaner och demokrater i kongressen. ”Ingen risk för nationell säkerhet? Baserat på vad?”, frågar den republikanske senatorn John Cornyn. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På måndagen meddelade Nvidia att Jensen Huang gör comeback som vd. Han avgick den 12 november efter avslöjanden om flera otrohetsaffärer, däribland en med en kvinna som misstänks ha kopplingar till kinesisk underrättelsetjänst. Enligt Nvidia fattades beslutet efter samtal med Huang och kontakter med högt uppsatta företrädare för den amerikanska regeringen. ” Utifrån dessa synpunkter är styrelsen övertygad om att återanställningen av herr Huang inte utgör någon risk för den nationella säkerheten ”, förklarade chipjätten i ett pressmeddelande. President Donald Trump var snabb med att ta åt sig äran. – Jag pratade med dem (Nvidias styrelse). Låt mig uttrycka det så här: Jag övertygade dem. Jag fick till uppgörelsen, sa han i en intervju med CNBC ett par timmar efter beskedet. Att Trump personligen lade sig i för att få Huang återinsatt möter kritik från både republikaner och demokrater i kongressen, rapporterar Axios . Flera ifrågasätter Nvidias bedömning att Huang inte utgör någon säkerhetsrisk.

articles.body_text: Storspionen Peyman Kia har begärt ut uppgifter om anställda inom Kriminalvården – och kräver nu en muntlig domstolsförhandling med tio vittnen. Samtidigt granskas hans handskrivna brev efter misstankar om att de innehåller kodade budskap. Spionen Peyman Kia uppger att han kämpar mot ”tortyrliknande” isolering på Kumla. Han kräver en förhandling i domstol om isoleringen och vill kalla Säpoanställda som vittnen. Kriminalvården misstänker kodade budskap till Rysslands militära underrättelsetjänst GRU. Begäran om personaldata väcker oro för att han ägnar sig åt kartläggning. Försöker den 47-årige Peyman Kia från Uppsala skicka kodade meddelanden till den ryska militära underrättelsetjänsten GRU, som var hans ”arbetsgivare”? Eller är Kriminalvården och Säkerhetspolisen alltför nitiska i sina bedömningar när de detaljgranskar de brev han skickar till myndigheter och domstolar? Har de gått för hårdhänt fram i besluten om att han ska hållas avskild från andra intagna på superfängelset i Kumla? Ett beslut som omprövas var tionde dag, vecka efter vecka, månad efter månad sedan den 7 december 2023 klockan 11.10 då det första beslutet togs. Svaren hänger i luften och döljs bakom olika paragrafer i sekretesslagen. Med hänvisning till rikets säkerhet får Peyman Kia enbart umgås med personalen som bevakar honom på Kumla. Inga interner tillåts komma i närheten. Nu vill han få stopp på den omfattande bevakningen på anstalten, som har pågått i snart tre år. I ett handskrivet brev till Förvaltningsrätten i Stockholm kräver Kia en muntlig förhandling i domstolen om sin isolering.

articles.title: Nya reglerna för turister i Alperna
articles.summary: Planerar du en naturskön vandring i de franska Alperna? Se då till att boka ditt besök i förväg – i alla fall om du ska till Chamonix. Från och med nästa år planeras besökskvoter vid flera populära sjöar med utsikt över Mont Blanc.
